items.title: Joint augmentation density relative to the input law times volume

source.anchor: Section 2.2, equations (2.6)-(2.7): joint-law density before inserting the Gibbs density of mu
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS mathematical restatement of the Gaussian joint-law component, not copied source prose or a claim of complete source-density formalization.

items.statement: For independent X with probability law mu and standard Gaussian Z on R^d, and eta>0, the joint law of (X,X+sqrt(eta) Z) equals mu(dx) q_eta(y-x) dy, where q_eta is the centered isotropic Gaussian density with variance eta. Inserting the paper's Gibbs density mu(dx)=Z_V^{-1} exp(-V(x)) dx is a separate final substitution to obtain the displayed joint Gibbs density.
assumptions: The paper works on R^d with d>=1 and a twice continuously differentiable potential with positive lower and upper Hessian bounds. Its target mu is the normalized Gibbs probability measure.
The source takes 0<eta<=1/beta and states the independent Gaussian augmentation X~mu, Z~N(0,I), Y=X+sqrt(eta) Z.
The selected intermediate identity is a density relative to mu tensor volume, rather than volume tensor volume. It needs only probability of mu and eta>0.

obligations.label: Identify the generative joint law with the explicit density relative to mu tensor volume
Insert the target's normalized Gibbs density to recover the density relative to volume tensor volume in (2.6)

bindings.boundary: Actual joint-law density relative to mu tensor volume only; source Gibbs-density substitution remains unbound and open. No reflection or PBPS-process claim.

assumption_deltas.source: The input is the paper's normalized smooth strongly log-concave Gibbs law on R^d
assumption_deltas.lean: Any probability measure mu on a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E
assumption_deltas.reason: The selected density is relative to mu tensor volume. Only the independent Gaussian coordinate is given a volume density, so mu may even be a Dirac measure. The missing Gibbs substitution is a separate obligation, not a hidden hypothesis.

assumption_deltas.lean: Every finite real dimension, including zero, with the canonical inner-product-space volume
assumption_deltas.reason: The proved noise-density parent and shear identity apply in zero dimension too. No arbitrary Haar normalization or extra measure-space parameter is introduced.
The upper bound is not used for the joint Gaussian-density identity; it belongs to other curvature and algorithmic statements.

assumption_deltas.source: Joint Gibbs density relative to dx dy, with the source's target-density definition
assumption_deltas.lean: Density relative to mu.prod volume, with factor q_eta(y-x)
assumption_deltas.reason: The actual Gaussian augmentation adapter is proved, but the final target-density and Gibbs-normalizer substitution is still outside this theorem and remains an unbound source obligation.

assumption_deltas.source: Independent sampling and translation of the Gaussian auxiliary coordinate
assumption_deltas.lean: Product probability measure, proved measurable factorization, explicit density transport, and shear preserving mu.prod volume
assumption_deltas.reason: The proof supplies the required measurable maps and product-measure contracts. Translation invariance is required only of volume, not of mu.
